chunks: And ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a mukātab for whom it is stipulated that if he is unable, then he is returned to slavery, and he became unable before paying anything.

He said: “He is not returned to slavery until three years have passed for him, and from him is emancipated in proportion to what he has paid as an installment. So when he has paid an installment, they have no right to return him to slavery.”

key_terms.الرِّقِّ: the state of slavery or bondage
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: a slave who has entered a contractual agreement to earn emancipation through payment
key_terms.ثَلَاثُ سِنِينَ: a period of three years before return to slavery is effected
key_terms.صَدْرًا: an installment or partial payment in this context
key_terms.عَجَزَ: he became unable to fulfill the payment obligation
key_terms.مِقْدَارُ مَا أَدَّى: the amount corresponding to what he has already paid
key_terms.يُشْتَرَطُ: it is stipulated as a condition in the contract

ai.seo_question: What happens in Shia fiqh if a mukātab fails to make payments before completing the manumission contract?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the mukātab, a slave under a contract of emancipation. It states that failure to pay does not immediately restore full slavery, and that any amount already paid secures a corresponding degree of emancipation. The report highlights the protection of contractual manumission within Shia fiqh.
